I'll be honest, this is an extremely close, marginal review. If there was an indifferent option, that would describe my view perfectly.

Once you get past the story line and get properly into the endless part of the game where you can do whatever you want, it's actually quite an enjoyable, fairly therapeutic walking simulator, while also having plenty of challenges you have to get around.

As for the music, well, it fits the game but I don't think it's anything special.

The problem for me is everything you have to endure to reach that point. The story line itself is weird and frankly creepy, the unskippable cutscenes are more annoying than anything else, and the fact that you have to watch the credits TWICE, again without being able to skip. I remember that when I reached those points, I just wandered off and did other things, waiting for them to finish. In a sentence, this is more like a movie than a game.

And I haven't even mentioned the price so far. £49.99 is an awful lot of money for mostly watching cutscenes. I did get it at half price or thereabouts, and... I'm just about satisfied.

Overall, it's a no from me, but only just. If you can get it at half price or better, then that's fair enough. Just remember that there are still better, cheaper games out there.

While it looked like a decent adventure at first (one where there's enough nice bits to keep your interest peaked despite all the flaws) - unfortunately, the more I played the more it was evident that the gameplay formula doesn't hold up.

Quite a lot of players criticize the "UPS sim" part of the game, but personally I'm finding it being the only part that warrants any positive feedback. It's quite simple yet not shallow, and it's reasonably original - there's clearly no games exactly like it, and not that many games with the same broad scope.

Unfortunately, I'd give a hard pass for ALL other gameplay aspects. I can't really stomach well Kojima-styled story & setting - too pretentious with way too childish presentation. And I'm finding any combat-oriented activity in the game (mobs, shooting missions, etc) to be mind-numbingly bland. It's not "bad", just very boring, lacking any real challenge (even on max difficulty), and extremely repetitious. And the further you go through the game, the more of it is thrown your way, and a lot of such "story-related" encounters you can't avoid at all.

It's a fairly strange game that tries so hard to sit on two chairs at once - but while one part of it is reasonably original and even a bit unorthodox, the other part is thoroughly bland.

There's an interesting sci-fi story in here, but its on rails and your actions don't have any impact on it in a meaningful way. It a set story connected by a rich detailed world... of fetch quests. This alone wouldn't bother me as I like atmospheric games, I like a slow place, and I like narrative, but the combo in DS just doesn't work for me. I feel the killer here the combo of not being able to be involved in the story combined with gameplay that's designed to be lonely and detached. I felt myself trying to beeline from story point to story point, just to grind through, but eventually just realized I wasn't enjoying it enough to care anymore. I regret my purchase and I doubt I'll ever finish this game. Will wrap it up through youtube.

Despite my lifelong love for Kojima's dramatic flair and convoluted storytelling demonstrated in the MGS series, I was skeptical of this game's release. As a big PC gamer, I was thrilled when it came to Steam, but by then I had learned it's essentially a walking simulator. BOY, WAS I WRONG.

In simplest terms, Hideo Kojima has gamified "wall climbing". Remember scaling that mountain in Skyrim? Or wall jumping the cliffs around Iron Forge in WOW? It takes the fun of that idea, of 'defeating' the terrain, and turns it into a game. And I have to say, it's brilliant.

I can't stress enough that this is basically "wall climbing" gamified. Meaning, don't play this if you're in the mood for GTA. Play this is you're in the mood to jump over some rocks while narrowly avoiding falling off a cliff, while carry 10 crates or a dead body or something. All while Kojima does his best to mind-f#$% you.

The soundtrack is beautiful too. If you can, I'd suggest playing this on a big TV with a controller versus a monitor and a keyboard. It's designed as a "console" game, which really means it shines as a TV game. Try to enjoy it that way, if you can.

Other than FedEx sim, I really enjoy the view and the environment that I've been put in. Looking forward "trying" to understand the whole plot of the story and will update this review once I'm done with the game

edit (6.9.2021) : Finally finished the game, it was quite a beautiful yet confusing on how the story went probably I missed a few things here & there but the end hit me quite hard. But it was a fitting ending. The amazing soundtrack backing it made the whole scene emotional. I suggest taking your time playing this game than rushing through the whole game as it wont do much. The game was paced to be time consuming and can eat up 3 to 5 hours of gameplay even if its just one or two deliveries.

TLDR: FedEx sim , pretty good

This one was a surprise. One of the best video games I've ever played in regards to story. It is beyond good. The game mechanics is a "delivery service", sure...but they make it interesting, and the indirect interaction you get with other players is fun. In the end though, the story and mystery is absolutely phenomenal. I highly recommend this game...and the ending is just so well done. If you're into a good story, this is a must-buy. Tip: Don't spend too much time in chapters 1 and 2. 3 is where the game really starts to come into its own.

It drags you along, and honestly you don't really know what to expect. It slowly progresses and by walking, walking and walking it drags you further into a compelling story. It’s an interesting tail, as to why you walk and deliver packages. You will have beautiful moments and interesting encounters that will leave a lasting impression.

The gameplay lacks a certain kick at times, and likes to throw you into the wild. But that can also create its charm, it doesn’t want to sugarcoat everything. Mechanics can be a little bit gimmicky and you’ll get thrown into different user interfaces. Even with tips enabled, it takes a bit of time to get the hang of it.

The scenery is gorgeous, walking around in the open is impressive and leaves you in awe. After a while you will realize a sudden shift in motivation. You are not walking for delivering packages. You are walking for the story.

Great story.
Definitely see how some people might not enjoy this kind of gameplay, a lot of inventory management/walking and you may be punished for being unprepared. If you are into Lovecraftian type stuff and just mystery in general I highly recommend this. One thing I'll say is don't expect to understand what's going on even 10 hours in, and pay attention to what the characters are saying.
One of my all time favourite games.
